subject: Evaluation Success Blueprint — acceptance tests, exit gates, and tie-break criteria
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Shah <pshah@carepathhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Evaluation Success Blueprint — first draft

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As promised, attached is an initial draft of the Evaluation Success Blueprint — a compact MAP-style plan that ties acceptance tests to concrete exit gates and a short close timeline (8 weeks). Key things in this draft:

- Two acceptance tiers: "Smoke" (end-to-end happy path) and "Conformance" (30-day reliability sample and latency sampling).
- Exit gates with pass thresholds (concordance >= 88% on top-3 intents, 95th pct latency <= 850ms under pilot load).
- Regression signal checklist and rollback triggers if recall or latency regresses >5% from baseline.
- A mutual runbook for evidence collection (sample prompts, anonymized logs, and an automated smoke harness).

Attachments: evaluation_blueprint_v1.docx, latency_slo_matrix.xlsx (latency numbers and test harness instructions).

As next steps, can you confirm:
1) Stakeholders who will sign acceptance at CarePath (technical, clinical ops, procurement)?
2) Any additional regulatory evidence you need (audit log granularity, data residency proof)?
3) A preferred weekly cadence for quick syncs (15–30 min) to review evidence and unblock tests.

I looped in Marissa (CS lead) and Ben (solutions) to help operationalize the acceptance tests and find any gaps in the runbook.

Thanks — looking forward to your feedback.

Warmly,

--
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com

Attachment stubs: evaluation_blueprint_v1.docx (38KB), latency_slo_matrix.xlsx (12KB)

From: Priya Shah <pshah@carepathhealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T12:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation Success Blueprint — first draft

Camila,

Thanks — this looks comprehensive and close to what we had in mind. Two quick clarifications from our side:

1) Stakeholders: Clinical Ops (Priya Shah), Platform Engineering (Elliot Tran), Procurement (Karla Mendes) — I can make intros where needed.
2) Audit logs: we need at least 90 days of immutable request/response logs with request IDs to map to clinical cases. Is that covered?
3) Latency: 850ms 95th is reasonable, but if the pilot includes larger documents (PDFs), we may need a separate SLO for doc-heavy flows. Can you propose a doc-flow SLO?

Also — we'd like a short tie-break criterion in case the acceptance metrics are borderline (e.g., 86–88%). That could be a weighted review: if concordance is 86–88%, but human review passes on a 200-sample with >=92% correctness, accept with a 2-week extended trial. Thoughts?

-Elliot (cc'd) will coordinate the technical hookups.

Best,
Priya

-----Original Message-----
On Tue, Sep 21, 2026 at 9:12 AM Camila Reyes wrote:
> [initial plan attached]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Shah <pshah@carepathhealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-22T08:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation Success Blueprint — first draft

Priya / team — quick product perspective:

- We can add a second SLO row specifically for document-heavy flows. Proposed doc SLO: 95th pct <= 1.6s under batch size typical for your workflows (we'll baseline during the first week).
- Audit logs: Redwood can provide 90-day immutable logs via our private retention pipeline; we'll deliver a template export and a fiduciary hash for tamper-evidence. Need to confirm whether your compliance team wants HSM-based signing — if so we'll route to Security.
- Tie-breaker: Ben agrees with the weighted-review approach. Operationalize as: if concordance in 86–88% window, run a 200-sample blind human audit (stratified by intent) and require >=92% pass on those samples to move forward to a 2-week extended trial. If the human audit <92%, trigger a remediation sprint.

I've updated the attached latency_slo_matrix.xlsx to include the doc SLO and an initial test harness recipe.

- Ben
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment stub: latency_slo_matrix.xlsx (v2, 14KB)

From: Elliot Tran <elliot.tran@carepathhealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Shah <pshah@carepathhealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-23T10:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation Success Blueprint — first draft

Thanks, all. A few operational asks from Platform Engineering: 

1) We need an evidence folder structure and naming convention for exported traces so we can automatically map request IDs to clinical case IDs. Can you provide a sample export and a small script (python) that maps the fields?
2) For the 200-sample human audit, are you able to deliver a simple labeling UI export (CSV) and a reconciliation report template?
3) Timeboxed SLA for fixes during the extended trial: can we add a 48-hour response target for high-severity regressions and a 5-day remediation window for productionizing fixes?

If we can get those pieces in the runbook, we can sign off internally and schedule the first-week smoke tests for Oct 4–8.

Elliot
Platform Engineering, CarePath Health

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Shah <pshah@carepathhealth.com>, Elliot Tran <elliot.tran@carepathhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-24T15:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation Success Blueprint — acceptance tests, runbook updates and timeline

Priya / Elliot — thanks for the fast feedback; updated plan attached and I captured the operational asks below. Final proposal so you can route for internal sign-off: 

Mutual action items (owner / deliverable / target)
- Redwood: supply sample export & mapping script (python) + evidence folder convention (owner: Ben) — by 2026-09-28
- Redwood: provide labeling CSV template and reconciliation report scaffold for the 200-sample human audit (owner: Marissa) — by 2026-09-29
- Redwood Security: confirm immutable-log signing approach (HSM vs hash) and provide implementation notes (owner: Security Eng team) — TBD (aim: 2026-10-01)
- CarePath: confirm final signatories and provide procurement contact (owner: Priya) — by 2026-09-27
- Both: schedule weekly 20-min sync (Mon 9:00am PT) starting 2026-10-04 for smoke evidence reviews

Acceptance & Exit Gates (short):
- Smoke (week 1): end-to-end sample pass rate >= 92% on curated smoke set; basic latency checks (API 95th <= 850ms, doc-flow 95th <= 1.6s)
- Conformance (weeks 2–6): concordance >= 88% on stratified 30-day sample; anomaly rate < 2%
- Tie-breaker: concordance 86–88% -> run 200-sample blind human audit; if human audit >=92% accept with 2-week extended trial; else remediation sprint
- Cutover: Procurement sign-off + security evidence + three consecutive daily rolling samples meeting smoke criteria

SLA for pilot regressions: 48-hour response for Sev-1; 5 business day remediation target for fixes moving into production.

Attachments: evaluation_blueprint_v1.docx (rev A, with the tie-break rules annotated), latency_slo_matrix.xlsx (v2).

If that aligns I will request final sign-off from my manager and push a DocuSign routing for the mutual action plan.

Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com
